content.overview: The financial statements shall give a true and fair view of the state of affairs of the company or companies, comply with the accounting standards notified under section 133 and shall be in the form or forms as may be provided for different class or classes of companies in Schedule III. The Board of Directors of the company shall lay before the company at every annual general meeting the financial statements for the financial year. A company which has one or more subsidiaries shall prepare a consolidated financial statement of the company and of all the subsidiaries in the same form and manner as that of its own.
content.glance: Financial statements must give a true and fair view, comply with section 133 accounting standards and Schedule III, and be laid at the AGM; consolidated statements where there is a subsidiary.
content.study:
## Section 129 — Financial statement

**True and fair view.** Financial statements must give a true and fair view of the state of affairs, comply with accounting standards notified under section 133, and be in the form in Schedule III.

**AGM.** The Board lays the financial statements before the company at every annual general meeting.

**Consolidation.** A company with one or more subsidiaries prepares a consolidated financial statement in the same form and manner as its own, and lays it before the AGM, subject to exemptions.

**Deviation.** Deviation from an accounting standard must be disclosed with reasons and the financial effect.

Books of account are section 128; filing is section 137.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.body: Lay before AGM; prepare consolidated statements where there is a subsidiary.

examples.title: Subsidiary consolidation
examples.body: Company with a subsidiary prepares consolidated financial statements and lays them before the AGM. Educational illustration.

hypotheticals.question: Must every company prepare consolidated financial statements?
hypotheticals.analysis: Only a company which has one or more subsidiaries (subject to exemptions). Standalone true-and-fair and Schedule III duties apply to all.

misconceptions.trap: Treating books of account (s. 128) as the same as financial statements (s. 129).
misconceptions.correction: Section 128 is the keeping of books; section 129 is the form, standards and laying of financial statements.
